questions.text: You feel comfortable being the center of attention.
You often imagine how things could be in the future.
You follow your heart rather than your head when making decisions.
You prefer to keep your options open instead of deciding right away.
You prefer quiet, solitary activities over large social events.
You are more interested in concrete facts than in abstract theories.
You place a high value on logic and objectivity.
You like having a detailed schedule for your day.
You often speak before fully thinking through what to say.
You love exploring complex concepts and symbolic meanings.
You worry a lot about how your words affect others' feelings.
You are very spontaneous and adapt easily to sudden changes.
You need a lot of time alone to recharge your energy.
You trust your past experience more than your intuition.
You are able to remain detached and critical during a discussion.
You feel frustrated when things don't go as planned.
You strike up conversations with strangers without effort.
You easily get lost in your own thoughts and hypotheses.
You notice right away when someone in the group is upset.
You work better under deadline pressure.
In a group you listen more than you talk.
You immediately notice practical details that others miss.
You would rather be told an uncomfortable truth than a kind lie.
You finish things well before the deadline.
After an evening among people you feel energized.
You care more about the big picture than about individual details.
You would make an exception to a rule to avoid hurting someone.
You happily change plans if something more interesting comes up.
Unexpected phone calls make you uncomfortable.
You prefer precise instructions to general guidance.
In an argument you look first at who is right, then at how people feel.
It bothers you to leave a job half done.
You prefer working in a group rather than on your own.
Connections between seemingly unrelated things occur to you.
When someone brings you a problem you comfort them first and look for solutions after.
You put off decisions until you are forced to make them.
Before voicing an opinion you prefer to have thought it over in private.
You describe things as they are, without metaphors.
You judge an idea by how well it holds up, not by who proposed it.
You make lists and tick them off.
You think better by talking things through out loud with someone.
Questions without a definite answer attract you.
In a hard decision the impact on the people involved weighs heavily.
Your desk is in creative disorder.
Long parties drain you, even when you are enjoying yourself.
You only trust what you can verify directly.
You apply the same rule to everyone, even when it is harsh.
Before leaving on a trip you plan everything in detail.
In meetings you speak up readily, even when you are unprepared.
You prefer a new problem to invent over a familiar one to carry out.
An environment full of conflict drains you even when it does not involve you.
A trip with no itinerary strikes you as the best way to travel.
You would rather send a message than make a phone call.
You prefer improving something that works over starting from scratch.
You easily spot the inconsistency in an argument.
You prefer a decision already made to a possibility still open.
You get restless if you go too many days without seeing anyone.
You often sense where a situation is heading before it becomes clear.
You find it hard to give negative feedback, even when it is deserved.
You start more things than you finish.
In a crowded room you are happy to stay on the edges.
You remember concrete facts well: dates, figures, places.
It bothers you when a decision is made on gut feeling.
You keep the spaces you work in tidy.
You are the first to introduce yourself in a room of new people.
Repeating a procedure you already know well bores you.
You trust the impression a person makes on you more than their track record.
Rigid rules strike you mostly as an obstacle.
You prefer a few deep relationships to many acquaintances.
In discussions you bring people back to the hard data.
You can say no to a request without feeling guilty.
You feel uneasy when a plan changes at the last moment.
You have a wide circle of acquaintances rather than a few close friends.
When you read something you immediately look for the meaning behind the words.
You feel guilty when a decision of yours was right but hurt someone.
You enjoy improvising instead of following a plan.
After a day full of meetings you need a break on your own.
You are more at ease with practical tasks than with speculation.
In the criticism you receive you look at the content, not the tone.
You prefer to know in advance what your day will hold.
